stories.headline: Fantasy football stock watch: Boston among players rising; Hurts falling
stories.summary: Matt Bowen lists players who are ascending after one month of play and others trending in the wrong direction.
stories.body:
Four games into the 2026 NFL season, fantasy football managers are starting to get a better feel for their rosters. We see scheme trends developing that impact player upside and usage (both positively and negatively), which can lead to smarter decisions when setting our weekly lineups.

It's also a reminder that the summer hype -- and talk of breakout players -- doesn't always hit once the games are played. Those players we had up high on our draft boards? Some of them are barely hanging on in the lineup, while there are also players emerging at an accelerated rate who need to be in starting slots.

Below are four ascending players and four more who are trending in the opposite direction heading into the Week 5 slate of games.

Stock rising

Denzel Boston, WR, Cleveland Browns

I'd have Boston locked into my lineup as a high-ceiling WR3/flex given his route deployment and explosive-play potential. Boston has scored 12 or more points in three of four games, with a touchdown reception in two. Plus, he's seeing 5.5 targets per game with a route tree that is expanding.

The deep shots from quarterback Deshaun Watson show up on the tape, as Boston has seen eight targets on throws of 15 or more air yards, but the rookie can also uncover on slants, out routes and comebacks. Looking at his play speed and ball-tracking ability, I see big upside for Boston, with the Jets, Ravens and Titans up next.

Deebo Samuel Sr., WR, San Francisco 49ers

Samuel has scored at least 15 points in three of four games, and he is being used exactly how we thought he would be in Kyle Shanahan's offense.

In a tough Week 4 matchup versus the Denver defense, Samuel caught five passes for 26 yards and a touchdown and added 44 yards rushing on three carries, good for 18 fantasy points. Backfield alignments (and carries), screens, crossers and unders. Shanahan will use Samuel, who is a power strider, on concepts that give him a long runway and space to display his vision and physical play style.

Now, the Week 5 matchup versus the Seattle defense isn't ideal, but Samuel gets the Commanders and Falcons, who both rank in the bottom five against opposing wide receivers, in Weeks 6 and 7, respectively. Samuel is a WR3 in 12-team leagues, and the arrow is pointing up for the veteran in this offense.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Chicago Bears

The Bears' ability to dominate game flow and time of possession in the Week 4 win over the Jets boosted the totals for Monangai, who scored a career-high 28 fantasy points, rushing for 146 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries. He was really decisive with the ball.

Monangai saw seven goal-to-go carries in the game (converting two for touchdowns), while D'Andre Swift struggled in the low red zone. In addition, a second-half Swift fumble prompted coach Ben Johnson to roll with Monangai to close out the game.

With the Packers up next (a team allowing 29 PPG to opposing running backs), and a Bears system that features the run game as a foundational element, both Swift and Monangai should be viewed as viable starters in the RB2/flex range. And that could stick moving forward, depending on weekly matchups.

Malik Washington, WR, Miami Dolphins

We need to talk more about Washington as a potential WR3 in deeper leagues. He has scored 11 or more points in back-to-back games, and he's averaging seven targets per game. Pretty good numbers. And Washington's versatility in the Miami offense creates opportunities within the game plan.

Washington will see targets as an outlet for quarterback Malik Willis on boots and checkdowns, and he can separate from both slot and perimeter alignments. Plus, he is playing that "Deebo" role in Miami, aligning as an I-back to handle rushing attempts. Washington has at least one carry in each of his last three games, and Miami will also get him the ball on fly sweeps and swing screens.

The lack of touchdowns (zero on the season) lowers the upside for Washington, but the usage (27% team target share) and overall deployment give him a stable floor in his upcoming schedule (CIN, BYE, @NYJ).

Stock falling

Jalen Hurts, QB, Philadelphia Eagles

It has been a subpar start to the season for Hurts, who is scoring 16.8 fantasy PPG and averaging 178.3 passing yards. The lack of touchdown production as a runner is really lowering his fantasy ceiling. Hurts is rushing for 26.3 yards per game, but he has just one score on the ground and only two carries inside the 5-yard line. That's rough for managers who drafted Hurts based on his touchdown upside as a dual-threat player.

It doesn't help that the Eagles are banged up right now at critical skill spots, with DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley dealing with hamstring injuries. Starting right tackle Lane Johnson retired this week, center Cam Jurgens was traded, and the Eagles' offensive line currently ranks in the bottom five in both pass and run block win rate. Given these factors, in addition to the matchup against the tough Jaguars defense this Sunday in London, Hurts will be outside my top 10 QBs for Week 5.

Omarion Hampton, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

This one is tough for me because I was all-in on Hampton this summer as the lead back in Mike McDaniel's offense. However, Hampton is scoring 11.2 fantasy PPG, and we saw L.A. move to a true committee approach this past week in the loss to the Seahawks.

Hampton managed to save his day with a late touchdown in that one, finishing with 13.3 points on 11 touches, but it was Keaton Mitchell who saw the most action (15 touches), with Kimani Vidal also getting in the mix (seven touches). And that's my concern moving forward with Hampton, as his nine carries versus Seattle were a season low.

I understand the Chargers' coaches here, too. This team is off to a 0-4 start, which leads to personnel changes. I've seen it firsthand in the league. Hampton is averaging only 4.0 YPC this season, and he hasn't impacted the offense as a receiver (7.3 yards per game).

With another tough matchup in Week 5 versus the Broncos, managers should play Hampton only as a touchdown-dependent flex, and this Chargers backfield rotation could keep him there for a while.

Daniel Jones, QB, Indianapolis Colts

Jones was a candidate this summer as a possible matchup-based QB1 in 12-team leagues or as a starter in superflex formats. But Jones is scoring just 9.1 fantasy PPG, down from the 17.4 he posted in 2025. The movement traits (and rushing totals) are limited because of his recovery from the Achilles injury he suffered last season. Plus, without Alec Pierce (IR/heel), the Colts are missing that vertical element in the pass game, which squeezes the field for the quarterback.

Through four games, Jones is averaging 188.5 passing yards per game, and he's 1-for-5 on throws of 20 or more air yards. Plus, Jones has rushed for one score while averaging just 5.3 yards per game on the ground, and he has managed only three touchdown passes (compared with four interceptions).

Pierce is eligible to return from IR in Week 7, which would give this pass game a lift. But I still don't see enough here for Jones to be played as anything more than a bye-week fill-in in deeper superflex formats.

David Montgomery, RB, Houston Texans

I really wanted this Texans run game to go this season. The team traded for Montgomery and they also addressed the offensive line. Get the running back with the contact balance and the lateral agility to play downhill behind an upgraded front.

It's not happening here.

Montgomery did score 28.9 fantasy points in Week 1, but he had three touchdowns in that game versus Buffalo, while producing only 79 total yards on 23 touches. And the numbers have really declined over his last three games, with Montgomery averaging 2.5 YPC and only 38.3 yards from scrimmage. More importantly, Montgomery hasn't found the end zone since Week 1. The result? He scored just 5.2 fantasy PPG in Weeks 2-4.

I don't see enough movement up front from a Houston offensive line with a run block win rate of 70.9% (28th in the league), and Montgomery has seen only 10.3 touches per game over his last three. With his upcoming schedule (@TEN, @JAX, NYG), Montgomery is (at best) a touchdown-dependent flex option.

stories.headline: F1 cars to get software update after Malaysia 'bug' to prevent repeat at future races
stories.summary: Following last weekend's farcical formation lap at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, the FIA will introduce new wet-weather engine software in time for the United States Grand Prix later this month.
stories.body:
Following last weekend's farcical formation lap at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, the FIA will introduce new wet-weather engine software in time for the United States Grand Prix later this month.

The Bahrain Grand Prix, which was hosted at Malaysia's Sepang circuit, was the first wet race under F1's new power unit regulations in 2026 and revealed a considerable oversight in the FIA software that polices the deployment of electric power on each car.

Described as "totally unacceptable" and "horrible" by drivers, a bug in the software supplied to all teams by the FIA resulted in multiple cars losing power as they followed the Safety Car at slow speeds on the formation lap.

The bug resulted in multiple cars losing drive coming out of the slow Turn 9 corner as the software prevented the use of electric power at a point where the internal combustion engine was struggling at low revs to spool the turbo and regain full power.

Some drivers were able to return to a normal speed once the system reset itself, while others, such as Lewis Hamilton, had to pull to the side of the track to restart their power unit.

"The review concluded that some cars running on low engine RPM [Revolutions Per Minute] in certain circuit sectors where a 250kW [kilowatt] power reduction was applied experienced a loss of power beyond the original intent and that could not be recovered in those sectors," an FIA statement said ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.

Once the issue was detected, the start of the race was suspended for a second time as the FIA investigated the bug.

Within five minutes of the suspension of the race, the FIA had released updated software to all teams to address the problem.

Over the following 30 minutes, the FIA worked with the teams to ensure the software was properly installed on all cars, allowing racing to get back underway 48 minutes after the issue first became apparent.

- Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Valtteri Bottas cycles impressive 400km from Malaysia to Singapore Grand Prix: 'Snakes were pretty chill'

- Max Verstappen says F1 paddock 'less stressful' without Christian Horner

The same software issued to the teams during the suspension of the race in Malaysia will be in use at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix before a further update will be released ahead of the United States Grand Prix on Oct. 25.

Although the FIA countered suggestions the software had not been tested at all prior to Sunday's race, its investigation recommended additional testing be granted in the future.

"The review also recommended that measures would be implemented for testing of the software, recognising that opportunities for testing are limited, to make it robust as possible," the statement added. "The FIA , together with the teams and Power Unit Manufacturers (PUMs), will continue to strengthen Power Unit software testing and verification capabilities, enhancing the overall validation process through independent assessment and collaborative feedback, including input from the supplier of the standardised Electronics Control Unit (ECU).

"The FIA would like to address comments suggesting that the software had not been tested prior to its deployment. Before implementation, teams and Power Unit manufacturers conducted simulation exercises to validate the software package, which was subsequently tested in full-scale running during Free Practice 1 sessions at both the Belgian Grand Prix and the Dutch Grand Prix."

stories.headline: Max Dowman presented with three Guinness World Records after breakout Arsenal season
stories.summary: Max Dowman has added three Guinness World Records to his growing list of achievements despite not turning 17 until this coming December.
stories.body:
Max Dowman has added three Guinness World Records to his growing list of achievements despite not turning 17 until this coming December.

The Arsenal winger enjoyed a breakout season in 2025-26, making 13 senior appearances and scoring a memorable clincher in the Premier League against Everton.

That goal -- in which Dowman ran from his own half, beat two players and tapped into an empty net with Jordan Pickford having come up for a corner -- came with the youngster aged just 16 years and 73 days old, officially making him the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history.

Dowman had already broken another world record prior to that. At the age of 15 years and 308 days, he was introduced as a substitute in Arsenal's 3-0 win at Slavia Prague and became the youngest player ever to make a Champions League appearance.

In fact, no 15-year-old other than him has ever played in the competition.

There was more glory, and one more world record, to come. With Arsenal having won their first Premier League title since 2004, Dowman collected his winner's medal when he was 16 years and 144 days old -- the youngest ever to do so.

Phil Foden was the previous holder of the award, as he was part of Manchester City's 100-point team when he was just 17 years old.

Dowman narrowly missed out on a fourth world record last season having made his debut -- and won a penalty -- against Leeds United at 15 years and 235 days old, just under two months older than teammate Ethan Nwaneri was when he made his debut against Brentford in 2022.

- Mikel Arteta signs new four-year Arsenal contract

- Ian Darke's early Premier League impressions for all 20 teams

- Myles Lewis-Skelly, Estêvão, Yan Diomande make 2026 Golden Boy shortlist

The winger has carried his good form into this season, having scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 Carabao Cup win over Ipswich in September.

Mikel Arteta's side return from the international break with a repeat of the fixture in which Dowman made his debut: Leeds at home, on Saturday.

stories.headline: Saints trade ruckman to Cats, chase on for star Swan
stories.summary: Geelong have brokered a trade for St Kilda ruckman Rowan Marshall, further depleting the Cats' draft stocks as Swans defender Nick Blakey eyes a move.
stories.body:
St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No. 14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

Cats football boss Andrew Mackie on Monday indicated an unwillingness to part with their first-round pick for Marshall after the Saints asked for a player to be attached to the trade.

St Kilda football boss Lenny Hayes hailed the fair return for Marshall, who has played 177 AFL games since being a rookie pick at age 21.

"We are pleased to have achieved (adequate compensation) by bringing in another first round selection, alongside our existing pick at eight," Hayes said.

Geelong needed to bolster their ruck stocks, with Rhys Stanley retiring and 21-year-old Mitchell Edwards still finding his feet at the level.

The Cats are among five clubs eyeing Nick Blakey as the Swans defender tests the water for a possible trade.

The 2024 All-Australian was one of five players who served a club-imposed ban through the AFL finals for breaching the club's behavioural standards at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne.

The 26-year-old has since been linked to a move despite being signed to Sydney until 2031.

Swans list boss Chris Keane said the club had not been told Blakey was meeting with rival clubs this week, but remained in talks with his manager Robbie D'Orazio.

"As we sit here right now, these are all hypotheticals," he told Trade Radio.

"It's certainly not something we've actively pursued, and we feel confident that he could walk back into our footy club.

"But given the calibre of player that he is, and the fact that he is contracted for five more years, we feel like making any deal happen would be significantly challenging."

Blakey's preferred option is reportedly Geelong, but the Cats have limited draft capital after executing trades for Marshall and Essendon's Jordan Ridley.

North Melbourne have expressed interest for Blakey, whose father John played in the Kangaroos' 1996 and 1999 premierships across 224 club games.

Essendon are another suitor, with Blakey's former mentors Mark McVeigh and John Longmire joining the club and the Bombers boasting salary cap room following the exits of Zach Merrett and Ridley.

"We haven't had any indication off Nick's management that he's looking to leave Sydney," Essendon list boss Matt Rosa told Trade Radio.

"But certainly we've had some discussions internally and we'll continue to do that."

Blakey has reportedly already met with Gold Coast coach Damien Hardwick, while St Kilda are also expected to make contact.

Any trade for Blakey would likely need to be approved by a club board, given the ongoing police investigation into an alleged sexual assault at the hotel.

Swans vice-captain Isaac Heeney, star midfielder Chad Warner, tagger James Jordon and Blakey were interviewed by police but no charges have been laid.

Riley Bice, another Swan banned for round 24 and the finals campaign, is not being investigated.

In other developments, young Hawk Aidan Schubert has agreed to be traded to Gold Coast in a separate deal that is expected to allow Ben King join Hawthorn as a free agent.

The Suns' 72-hour window to match the Hawks' offer for King or accept compensation, likely pick No. 7 in the draft, ends at 4.15pm (AEDT) on Friday.

The Western Bulldogs are yet to file free agency paperwork for Port Adelaide's Zak Butters ahead of Friday afternoon's deadline.

Port can accept draft compensation, which would currently deliver pick No.5, or match the Bulldogs' offer and force a trade.

The trade period closes on Wednesday evening.

stories.headline: Silva rises in P4P women's top 10, making most of golden opportunity
stories.summary: After winning UFC women's flyweight title, Silva rises in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
The women's flyweight division might be the most stacked weight class in the UFC, and Natalia Silva wears the gold.

Silva was too fast, too precise and too elusive for Wang Cong in the UFC 332 main event on Saturday, and as a result, the 29-year-old from Brazil captured the vacant 125-pound title. She moves up one position to No. 4 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

Silva is one of seven flyweights in the women's top 10. The division with the next most pound-for-pound elites is lightweight, with three fighters in the men's rankings.

The top two fighters on the women's list are Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the UFC title last month while healing shoulder and back injuries, and Zhang Weili, a two-time former strawweight titlist who last fought at flyweight, in an unsuccessful challenge of Shevchenko in November.

Aside from Silva, there are three other UFC flyweights in the top 10 (Alexa Grasso, Manon Fiorot and Erin Blanchfield), and the rankings also include PFL 125-pounder Dakota Ditcheva.

UFC women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has been missing from these rankings for the past few months because, with no fights since June 2025, she is ineligible. But Harrison will return from neck surgery to defend her title against former two-division champion and consensus GOAT Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Nov. 14.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Oct. 7. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which Natalia Silva captured by beating Wang Cong at UFC 332. When Shevchenko is healed up, she'll be looking to take back the belt.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Previous ranking: 4

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her upcoming bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: How to bet Bucs-Cowboys on TNF: Analysis, tips and top prop plays
stories.summary: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys on "Thursday Night Football."
stories.body:
The Dallas Cowboys head into Week 5 at 2-2, coming off a 34-30 win in Houston. Dak Prescott is playing at an extremely high level for an explosive Cowboys offense, completing 70% of his throws (fourth highest in the league), while running this system like a point guard. CeeDee Lamb, who had a career-high 17 receptions (on 21 targets) in the win over Houston, paces the wide receivers room, while George Pickens offers big-play ability on the perimeter. Javonte Williams is the downhill hammer in the run game for a unit that is scoring 30.5 PPG. The defense, under new coordinator Christian Parker, has yet to form its 2026 identity, allowing 28.0 points and 389.5 yards per game, which both rank in the bottom five of the league. But this group has the talent -- and the scheme -- to match up with a Tampa Bay Buccaneers offense that will be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb).

The 0-4 Buccaneers started undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels in the Week 4 loss to the Packers. We saw a lot of quick-game concepts, screens and defined reads for Daniels, but he did make some throws while bringing an added element as a dual-threat player on designed carries and scrambles (eight rushes, 55 yards). The Buccaneers will look to control tempo with Bucky Irving and the ground game against a Dallas defense surrendering 150.3 rushing yards per game (second most in the league), while the passing game will need to generate more vertical throws for Daniels. On defense, we know Todd Bowles' unit will try to heat up Prescott (38.2% blitz rate) with more zone coverage in the secondary to limit explosive plays over the top.

Betting outlook

I'm going to follow the trends and what we've seen from both clubs over the first four weeks of the season. As I mentioned before, the Bucs set up Daniels last week with throws that allowed him to make quick reads and play as a ball distributor in his first pro start. That should continue against a Dallas defense that has struggled to limit opposing quarterbacks (239.9 passing yards per game). And Irving should play a volume role on the ground.

The same can be said for Lamb and his consistent usage in the pass game (at least eight targets in each game). Look for throws that target coverage voids, which increase his numbers Thursday night. I like the Tampa Bay defense to hold Javonte Williams' yardage totals in check, though he might find the end zone. The Buccaneers are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per game.

Game bets: Dallas -8.5 (-115), total points OVER 47.5 (-115)

I'm taking Dallas at home to cover versus a Bucs team that has lost 13 straight games against the spread. Dallas has too many explosive playmakers here. And I think Christian Parker's defense can create enough impact plays versus the rookie quarterback to win by two scores. Looking at the total, the Cowboys have hit the over in 10 straight games. I do see this Tampa route tree expanding in Daniels' second pro start, and we know Dallas can both score and give up points.

Notable player props, bets

Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

Bucky Irving rushing yards OVER 51.5 (-115)

Irving has rushed for at least 61 yards in two of his last three games, with at least 15 carries in all three. It's a positive matchup here, and Tampa needs to run the ball.

stories.headline: Fantasy basketball: André Snellings' Ultimate Draft Board
stories.summary: André Snellings crunches the numbers, factors in average draft position and highlights the best spots to draft key players throughout your fantasy basketball draft.
stories.body:
What does your perfect fantasy basketball draft look like?

This is a question you should consider before your draft begins, when you're still in the planning stages. Even now, after all these years of playing fantasy sports, I still do this before most big drafts.

I look at where I'm picking in the draft and decide who, among those likely to be there, I'll take first. Then I'll look at where my next picks will be and compare that to the player rankings, to see who I would most want among players in the right range for me to potentially take them.

Having that plan in place can help you enter your fantasy basketball draft with a clearer idea of what you want to accomplish. Most of the people in your leagues aren't going to go into the draft with much of a plan and will instead just hope for the best. So, if you step into the draft with an idea about what the talent looks like at different parts of the draft, it will give you a leg up on the competition right from the opening tip.

The best way to gauge what your team might look like, in my experience, is to do mock draft(s) before my real drafts to get a feel for what players should be available. Will my sleeper picks be there, or does everyone know about them so they go earlier than expected?

Often, there are really good players ranked lower than you might expect that might be available later than you think they should be. Having an idea of how this tends to shake out before you enter your draft can be very valuable for maximizing your squad.

In this article, I highlight players I would like to draft at different locations within the draft. In the early rounds, draft slot makes a huge difference in what players might be available, so I point out players of interest in different parts of the round.

In the middle and later rounds, I highlight groups of players that I like that should be available in that range.

To determine likelihood of availability, I utilize Average Draft Pick (ADP) data to offer insight on the type of value that might be available throughout your own drafts.

Note: ADPs are current as of date of publish. Click here for the latest.

The foundation
Round 1: Still playing the Joker card

If I have the first pick in a points league, I'm taking Nikola Jokic (ADP 1.5) immediately. He has been the top fantasy scorer for six straight seasons, and has averaged a triple-double in two straight. He not only projects as the top player this season, but is projected to outscore second place by more than 500 fantasy points. That's larger than the gap between the bottom of the first round and a mid-late fourth round pick.
In category leagues, there is a legitimate debate whether to take Jokic or Victor Wembanyama (ADP 3.1) first. Wembanyama's league-leading shot-blocking is very valuable in category leagues, and with his strong across-the-board contributions and ever-improving game (he is still only 22 years old!) he is a justifiable top pick even over the dominant Jokic.
In points leagues, Giannis Antetokounmpo (ADP 5.7) and Jalen Johnson (ADP 8.7) project as strong mid-round picks. Both play similar do-everything-power-forward positions that produce strong counting volume in several categories. However, both are better in points than category leagues. Giannis, in particular, shoots a high volume of free throws at a low percentage that is Shaq-like kryptonite in category leagues. In the mid-first of category leagues, I'm hoping for Anthony Edwards (ADP 7.2).
At the end of the first round, I'm aiming at Jayson Tatum (ADP 9.2) in both formats. There are some health questions in his first full season back after his torn Achilles, but if he is in form he could be in for the type of glow-up that former teammate Jaylen Brown had last season. Tatum should be the focal point for the Celtics in a way he never could be when Brown was on the squad.

Round 2: Mitchell, Maxey, Sabonis or three PGs if they slide to the second

In the middle of the second, the top options per league-type are the non-point guards. Domantas Sabonis (ADP 16.9) is a borderline first-round talent when healthy in points leagues, while Cooper Flagg (ADP 17.4) is strong value in the middle of the second round of category leagues. And Flagg has almost limitless upside in his second NBA season, still only 19 years old, on a Mavericks team that should play much more to his strengths in this campaign.
At the end of the second, I'm back to the point guards. Trae Young (ADP 22.7) and Josh Giddey (ADP 23.3) project as mid-second rounders in points leagues. Tyrese Haliburton (ADP 19.2) projects as a mid-second rounder in category leagues in his return from a torn Achilles in 2025.

Round 3: Rockets early, LaMelo and the OGs late

The Houston Rockets have three players that project as either late-second or early third rounders in Kevin Durant (ADP 19.5), Amen Thompson (ADP 20.2) and Alperen Sengun (ADP 24.2). Any of the three would be worthy picks early in the third.
LaMelo Ball (ADP 25.6) was traded to the Timberwolves this offseason to pair with Anthony Edwards, and it could be a perfect match. Ball's circus style of highlight assists and logo 3-pointers have been badly needed in Minnesota, and if he stays healthy he could be in for his best season.
James Harden (ADP 28.3) and Anthony Davis (ADP 31.8) are ultra veterans that still have third-round projection grades. Davis is always a durability risk, and he is in a new location with the Wizards, but if he's healthy he is a borderline first round talent that is worth the risk by the end of the third round.

Round 4: Avdija, Reaves and White

Deni Avdija (ADP 35.0) exploded in a career effort last season; he was one of the leading candidates for NBA Most Improved Player until after the All-Star break. He is the face of the youth movement of the Trail Blazers and remains the focal point of their offense.
Austin Reaves (ADP 39.6) will have an even larger role for the Los Angeles Lakers this season after the departure of LeBron James. He should produce big stats on a daily basis next to Luka Doncic, and if Doncic sits Reaves has limitless upside. In four games without Doncic and James last season, Reaves averaged 39.0 PPG, 9.5 APG and 4.8 RPG.
Derrick White (ADP 40.3) is the most under-the-radar fantasy star in the league. He ranked 19th in the Player Rater last season, and projects to top-40 in points leagues and top-20 in category leagues. He is outstanding value if he slides to the fourth round in category leagues.

Middle rounds (Rounds 5-8)

Mikal Bridges (ADP 51.9) is the poster child for the expression "the best ability is availability". Bridges has never missed a game in the NBA, and that gives him a hefty games advantage over most NBA players. He almost always outproduces this draft range.
Nickeil Alexander-Walker (ADP 55.7) fit perfectly in his first season with the Hawks and won the NBA Most Improved Players. His projected value is about 10 slots above his draft position.
Dyson Daniels (ADP 60.4) is a defensive specialist with a developing offensive game that projects him to top-50 in points leagues and top-40 in category leagues.
Naz Reid (ADP 66.3) was the centerpiece that the Charlotte Hornets got back in exchange for Ball, and he could be in for a big season. His defense and 3-point shooting with double-double potential projects him into the top-60 of points leagues and the top-40 category leagues.
The Lakers traded for Walker Kessler (ADP 79.0) to be their franchise big man. He is one of the best shotblockers in the league, which makes him a strong category producer when healthy. He projects as a top-50 player in that format.

Late rounds (Round 9 and beyond)

Ty Jerome (ADP 93.8) is coming off an amazingly efficient season with the Memphis Grizzlies. He missed much of the season injured, but in the 15 games he played he averaged 19.7 PPG and 5.7 APG in only 22.6 MPG. For perspective, that translates to 31.3 points and 9.0 assists per 36 minutes. If his role with the Grizzlies is larger this season, he could produce a big season.
Ivica Zubac (ADP 94.6) had career efforts in his last two campaigns with the LA Clippers before injuries slowed him down. This season, now healthy and playing next to elite point guard Haliburton with the Indiana Pacers, Zubac should be back to his double-double ways.
Paul George (ADP 105.0) is purely a lottery ticket. His durability for the past several seasons has lowered his fantasy value, but now he is playing with the Celtics in a version of Jaylen Brown's old role. While he's on the court, he will have major 3-point and scoring volume upside.
Kel'el Ware (ADP 107.6) could be in for a much bigger role this season. Ware was traded to the Bucks as part of the package for Giannis Antetokounmpo, and will have the chance to play himself into starter minutes. With is 3-point range and shotblocking ability, Ware has big upside in category leagues.
Darius Acuff Jr. (ADP 108.0) and Darryn Peterson (ADP 109.0) are both high-volume rookies likely to play major roles on rebuilding teams. Both will have to learn to score efficiently at the next level, but both have 20+ PPG upside even as first year players.
Jalen Green (ADP 114.8) was the leading scorer for the Rockets two seasons ago, then battled injury all last season. Still only 24 years old, Green has 25+ PPG upside if he settles more fully into his role in his second campaign with the Suns.

stories.headline: Valtteri Bottas cycles impressive 400km from Malaysia to Singapore Grand Prix: 'Snakes were pretty chill'
stories.summary: Valtteri Bottas rode past snakes, jumped over a lizard and got chased by a dog during a four-day, 418 kilometre bike ride from Malaysia to Singapore ahead of this weekend's Formula 1 race.
stories.body:
Valtteri Bottas rode past snakes, jumped over a lizard and got chased by a dog during a four-day, 418 kilometre bike ride from Malaysia to Singapore ahead of this weekend's Formula 1 race.

While a flight from Kuala Lumpur to Singapore often nudges just over an hour duration, Bottas opted for a slightly unconventional journey instead.

The Cadillac driver posted daily updates of the journey to his Strava account. On day one, he cycled 56.60km, before logging 161km on day two along the coast past Malacca City. On day three he did another 161km and then a final 40.16km to finish the route on Wednesday.

Bottas joked the stifling heat had made his bike seat like a "cheese grinder" but said the ride will not have set him back in his preparations for the Singapore Grand Prix.

"I obviously wouldn't do it if I knew it hurt my preparation," he said. "So, for sure, I'm pretty good. The amount of sweat in those days was quite impressive. But yeah, definitely, you get used to the heat the more time you spend in the heat, so that can help me hopefully a little bit [this weekend]."

While Bottas cycled solo, he said he had a recovery vehicle following him to ensure he did not hit any trouble.

Asked what his best experiences were, Bottas told the media on Thursday: "Saw some snakes, which I was a little bit worried about, but actually they were pretty chill. They were just doing their thing. I saw one cobra. Saw one python just crossing the path in front of me. Saw some of those big lizards that you also see here.

"One was on the path, I had to jump over it with a bike. So I saw it like last minute. Got chased by one dog. Got stuck behind a group of cows on a small track. Eventually they moved away. What was the wildest part was the riding at night in the jungle.

"The noise in there is like ... Then your mind starts to play games of what is out there. Who knows what is out there, but then you just need to crack on and keep going. Riding with your lights at night, that was probably the most epic part in the forest."

- Max Verstappen says F1 paddock 'less stressful' without Christian Horner

- Mercedes confirm George Russell engine penalty at Singapore Grand Prix

- Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

His journey went viral this week, with F1 media accounts sharing daily updates from his Strava posts.

"I was surprised how big it became," he admitted. "But if people follow me on my activities, they know that it's not like something super extreme to me. I love the endurance stuff anyway."

Bottas' route was inspired to him by his wife, Australian Olympic cyclist Tiffany Cromwell.

He said: "I think Tiffany mentioned it as kind of like a joke, 'hey, you could just ride from there, it's not that far.' And then I was like, 'hmm, maybe, I could.' I obviously had to check the distance, how the roads are, the timings, and then just made a solid plan for each day. All the routes were planned."

Bottas' journey started on Sunday after the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia -- the Sepang circuit was a late entry to this year's schedule after Bahrain's race was cancelled due to the war in the Middle East.

Bottas intentionally planned the two longest days on Monday and Tuesday so he could have a recovery ride on Wednesday. He has another rest day Thursday before Friday, which features a one-hour practice session and then qualifying for Saturday's sprint race.

It might be a one-off opportunity to do the ride, with Malaysia not on the calendar in 2027 -- although sources have told ESPN talks have started about a potential return in 2030, spurred on by the goodwill generated by its Bahrain stand-in appearance.

Asked if he ever might do something similar, Bottas said: "When I got to the hotel yesterday afternoon, I said to myself, but no, not again.

"But now, today, I'm like, yeah. Let's see."

stories.headline: Ian Darke's early Premier League impressions for all 20 teams
stories.summary: Might Arsenal be more vulnerable than expected? Are Brighton capable of making a top-four bid? Here's what stands out from the first weeks of Premier League action.
stories.body:
The Premier League is back this weekend with all eyes on crisis-torn Manchester City as they go to Liverpool, of all places.

Here is a first indication of how City and their players react to the bombshell news that they have been found guilty of 114 out of 115 charges of breaking financial rules over a long period. Will that mean relegation or a huge points deduction? Is that a de-motivating factor for the players, whose future now looks uncertain? Or will they come out fighting?

City still protest their innocence and are appealing the verdict, but this leaves a huge cloud hanging over their past and present. Their season will progress in a strange vacuum, with opposing fans calling them "cheats" at every away game. Enzo Maresca's team is 100% so far, without being wholly convincing.

- How top Premier League clubs view Man City's guilty verdict

- Should Carrick be feeling the heat on another bad Man Utd run?

- Which managers could fit Man Utd, Spurs if needed this season?

In any case, it is way too early to jump to conclusions about this Premier League season. A year ago, Liverpool were top with a 100% record, but they faded by season's end and finished fifth. Tottenham Hotspur were third last September, then ended up needing a win on the final day to avoid relegation. Aston Villa were in the drop zone, yet ultimately finished in the top four.

All of that should serve as a reminder that the action so far this season only represents the opening chapter of what we hope will be a rather good book. Teams that are struggling now, such as Manchester United and Chelsea, might find a winning rhythm, while early pace-setters such as Brighton & Hove Albion and Hull City could find that things get tougher when injuries, suspensions or a rough run of games kick in.

All we can truthfully report are some first impressions. Here's what I've noticed about each Premier League team over the early weeks of the season.

Arsenal
The defending champions looked almost invincible in their first few games until the embarrassing 3-0 loss at Brighton. Was it a blip or a sign that they are vulnerable?

It was their fourth away game in 10 days, so that is a mitigating factor. And they were playing a team at the top of their game, in addition to looking off the pace themselves. But as manager Mikel Arteta hinted, there was also a touch of complacency in that display and that is something they will need to guard against.

The loss has knocked them off the top of the table, but it will be interesting to see if days like this become a part of their DNA. Leeds United at home is next, and that will be a good test.

Manchester City
Has the heart been ripped out of Manchester City? Nobody inside or out of the club can possibly know what lies ahead, or how it might affect performances. Sunday's trip to Anfield will offer clues. Head coach Enzo Maresca could not have made a better start after succeeding Pep Guardiola, but is walking into unknown territory. Reports that Erling Haaland felt fatigued during the international break do not help, either.

On the pitch, things appear a bit brighter. New signings Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Iliman Ndiaye have made great starts and the 1-0 win at Old Trafford in the Manchester derby, albeit with a goal that should not have stood, was a test passed for Maresca, whose City side executed a cute tactical display when down to 10 men.

Liverpool
Of course, Liverpool -- like several teams under new bosses -- are a work in progress, with two wins and three draws. This team is still adapting to the manic high-press tactics favored by coach Andoni Iraola. Things are starting to click, and club-record striker Alexander Isak is looking his old self at least, with four goals already.

The Reds do not really look like title contenders at this early stage, but that City game on Sunday will be informative. Iraola has solved the right back problem with Ronald Araújo, on loan from Barcelona, but Milos Kerkez still looks shaky on the left side of a defense in which young center back Jérémy Jacquet looks a real find.

Chelsea
What about the other supposed Big Six teams? Chelsea were awful at Brentford in their 3-0 loss on Sept. 18, and they look soft and sloppy defensively.

Despite a superb attacking trio of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and João Pedro (how on earth did Brazil leave him out of their World Cup squad?), coach Xabi Alonso has some big problems to solve. They have taken just one point from the last nine available, and preseason predictions of a title challenge look way off the mark.

Manchester United
Where has all of last season's momentum gone at Manchester United? Coach Michael Carrick seemed to have cracked the code as they climbed up to third place, but all the dynamism and belief has mysteriously disappeared this season, and it is hard to know why.

I think they miss Casemiro's presence in midfield, despite investing heavily in that area in the summer. Youri Tielemans has proven pedigree, but Andrey Santos -- who hardly got a kick at Chelsea and signed for £48 million, has quickly lost his place at United, who do not have money to waste.

Is the infrastructure not good enough? Why was no left back brought in? The team just look undercooked so far. Carrick would not panic in a hurricane, and there are enough good players that we should expect their form to return. But United are already out of a title race their fans dream of contesting again one day.

Tottenham Hotspur
Just when you thought things could only improve for Spurs, they got even worse; bottom of the table after a £300 million outlay in the transfer window is embarrassing. And their first two league goals of the season against Aston Villa came too late to rescue the game.

To be fair, there have been signs of something better in recent games, and they have not had much luck. But you wonder if there is something of a psychological block at work, too. I will go out on a limb here and say coach Roberto De Zerbi will get Spurs going, but he has to find more game time for gifted and now-fit playmaker James Maddison.

Brighton & Hove Albion
Elsewhere, Brighton have been a revelation -- so much so that one or two observers have wondered whether coach Fabian Hürzeler's team can "do a Leicester" and mount a surprise title challenge. With European competition to cope with as well, it looks unlikely.

Teenage striker Charalampos Kostoulas is catching the eye, while 35-year-old midfielder Pascal Gross has to be one of the shrewdest and best-value signings in Premier League history. Brighton have signed him twice, the second time for only about £1.7 million from Borussia Dortmund, and he is bossing matches in midfield. Top four is not out of the question.

Rest of Premier League
- Brentford draw rather too many games, but they remain a tough nut to crack and nobody has so far. Manager Keith Andrews has a gifted and highly motivated band of brothers.

- Likewise, Leeds United remain unbeaten and are all set to build on last season's promising first year back in the big time. A mention here for their unsung captain Ethan Ampadu, who rarely misses a game and is a key leader in the midfield. Credit manager Daniel Farke for at last keeping striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin fit again. The move to Elland Road has been fantastic for the former Everton man.

- Everton are also yet to taste defeat despite a nightmarish transfer deadline day, leaving them with a squad that looked too thin. The Toffees have kept four clean sheets in six matches now that Jarrad Branthwaite has returned to the defense, so no wonder David Moyes is smiling a little more. But he will need January reinforcements if Everton are to realize their target of a return to Europe.

- Aston Villa have had the heart of their team ripped out -- Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martínez are among their many notable departures. But there are signs already that Unai Emery is starting to rebuild successfully, helped by a good UEFA Champions League win at Club Brugge.

- Newcastle United bounced back from a dreadful 4-1 thrashing at Leeds to beat Hull City. That was important because they looked so lightweight at Elland Road. The verdict so far for this new-look Toon is "satisfactory work and progress," but it will be a surprise if they finish in the top half this time around.

- The Thursday-Sunday routine of European games will make it hard for AFC Bournemouth, still without a league win, and Sunderland, though their lively displays against Arsenal and Man City suggest they will cope.

- Hull City, tipped by almost every pundit to go down, continue to snarl defiance. Coach Sergej Jakirovic has 18 new players and, starting with a win over Manchester United, performances have been a tribute to their fight and organization. The boss is realistic enough to know that 40 points and survival is the only game in town, but the Tigers are giving themselves a decent chance of achieving their goal.

- Of the other promoted clubs, Ipswich Town are lively enough in attack and will be happy with a midtable start, and Coventry City's first win at Nottingham Forest will give them belief they can compete at this level, especially since Frank Lampard's side put in a good shift in losing only 1-0 to Manchester City as well.

- Fulham still cannot win, but young attackers Gonzalo García and Josh King give them hope, and David Affengruber's arrival from Elche in Spain has helped to tighten a porous defense.

- It has been a slow start to the season for Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest and the laconic Pierre Sage's Crystal Palace, but both are good enough to stay afloat.

stories.headline: Brewers eliminate Padres with 3-1 win in Game 4, advance to NLCS rematch with Dodgers
stories.summary: — Garrett Mitchell tripled and scored the tiebreaking run in the fifth inning before making a pivotal catch on Manny Machado's drive to the wall in the eighth, and the Milwaukee Brewers advanced to the National League Championship Series for the...
stories.body:
SAN DIEGO -- — Garrett Mitchell tripled and scored the tiebreaking run in the fifth inning before making a pivotal catch on Manny Machado's drive to the wall in the eighth, and the Milwaukee Brewers advanced to the National League Championship Series for the second straight season with a 3-1 victory over the San Diego Padres on Wednesday night, winning their best-of-five Division Series in four games.


Mitchell also drove in Sal Frelick with Milwaukee’s first run as the Brewers snapped their 12-game postseason road losing streak since 2018 and reached the team's fifth League Championship Series.


Machado nearly tied Game 4 with a 406-foot drive off reliever Abner Uribe, but Mitchell coolly tracked it down and reached just above the short wall in right-center to keep it in the yard.


Second baseman Brice Turang then ended the eighth with an acrobatic catch of Ty France’s tailing popup in foul ground.


After fending off the surging Padres in four tight games decided by a combined five runs, the 103-win Brewers will get an NLCS rematch with the Los Angeles Dodgers, who eliminated Atlanta on Wednesday.


The Dodgers swept Milwaukee last October on the way to their second consecutive World Series title.


Fernando Tatis Jr. hit a 429-foot homer on an otherwise tepid offensive night for the Padres, who repeatedly tested the majors’ best regular-season team before falling short of only the fourth NLCS appearance in team history.


One night after the Padres avoided elimination in Game 3, Milwaukee claimed its first road playoff win since the 2018 NLCS by sticking to its season-long formula for success.


While four Brewers pitchers combined on a three-hitter and the defense made nearly every big play, Milwaukee’s lineup calmly worked counts, pounded 10 hits through the Padres' defense and manufactured enough runs to head home smiling.


Game 2 hero Jackson Chourio capped his high-impact series by driving in Mitchell to become the Brewers’ career leader in postseason RBI at just 22 years old. Chourio has 17 RBI, including six in this series, in 16 playoff games.


Milwaukee opened the scoring in the third when Frelick reached on an infield single, stole second and came around on a single by Mitchell, an Orange County native and UCLA product.


Brewers starter and former Padres draft pick Robert Gasser threw four innings of three-hit ball, but Tatis ended his 1-for-19 skid since San Diego's playoff opener with a long shot to center in the third. It was the longest homer ever hit in the postseason at Petco Park by a San Diego player.


Padres starter Walker Buehler yielded just three hits and a run, but manager Craig Stammen replaced him with Game 1 starter Robbie Ray after William Contreras’ leadoff single in the fourth.


Mitchell then stroked a mild liner perfectly over first base and into the right-field corner leading off the fifth, and he scored on Chourio's single through the drawn-in infield. Chourio surpassed Ryan Braun for the most postseason RBI in Brewers history.


Jake Bauers singled leading off the sixth and went to third on Cooper Pratt's ground-rule double before scoring on Frelick's sacrifice fly.


The Padres were already down 3-1 in the seventh when Mason Miller allowed three baserunners, but no runs. The vaunted closer missed Game 3 for the birth of his first child.


After sitting below .500 and in 11th place in the NL in late July, San Diego roared into the first wild-card spot and then swept the Cubs in the Wild Card Series last week. The Padres had won 19 of 22 before losing three of four to Milwaukee.


Up next
The Brewers host the Dodgers in Game 1 on Sunday with ace Jacob Misiorowski almost certainly lined up to start. Milwaukee is four wins from only the second World Series berth in team history.
